races.name: Rob Over The Hill EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Battle Fever
runners_data.comment: A £50,000 son of Sands Of Mali and half-brother to a modest performer at six furlongs, out of a dam without much to recommend her at five, he's from a yard short on form currently but with a strong record in this event, having been successful in it last year; a booked rider with a fine record at the track is a plus, though he otherwise looks up against it on debut, and a rating of 67 reflects a middling profile.

runners_data.name: Desert Move
runners_data.comment: Having been well beaten on a modest debut in a maiden at Hamilton, he drops significantly in trip to five furlongs today, which could bring about improvement, for a yard that has landed two of the last five runnings of this race; drawn wide, he carries a workable rating of 72 with room to progress.

runners_data.name: Enemy Action
runners_data.comment: He found things tougher when stepped up to six furlongs, finishing down the field in a seller at York last time, but dropping back to this shorter trip, regarded as his more effective range, could bring improvement, though there's still more for him to find; drawn wide, a rating of 74 keeps him in this mix as a value danger.

runners_data.name: Inca Warrior
runners_data.comment: By Invincible Army and a half-brother to a modest performer over seven furlongs, he's tough to fancy with any confidence on debut, especially with connections without a success from their last 22 runners; a rating of 67 reflects a workmanlike profile at best.

runners_data.name: Palm Reader
runners_data.comment: A costly breeze-up purchase by Blue Point out of a dam smart over six furlongs, he wears a tongue-tie for the first time and faces a stiff task on debut against more experienced rivals; a rating of 67 is respectable enough without making him easy to fancy.

runners_data.name: Up The Stakes
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on a substandard debut in a novice at Newcastle, his only start so far, he has everything still to prove and sits at the bottom of these figures on a rating of just 42, leaving him hard to consider without more encouraging signs.

runners_data.name: Waiting For Archie
runners_data.comment: A big, raw sort who ran to a similar level as his debut when beaten eight and a quarter lengths over seven furlongs in a maiden at Leicester last time, he's bred to appreciate more of a test than today's drop in trip and is drawn wide; his yard has landed two of the last five runnings of this race, but a rating of 64 leaves him with more to prove.

runners_data.name: Autumn Jewel
runners_data.comment: Effectively still finding her feet, she was well beaten on a truncated debut effort in a maiden at Musselburgh, and clear improvement is needed to be competitive here, though she is bred with plenty of speed and wears a hood for the first time; a rating of 65 leaves her towards the rear of these figures.

runners_data.name: Nightbloom
runners_data.comment: A serious pedigree on show, being a 400,000-euro daughter of Invincible Spirit, half-sister to a high-class sprinter, and out of a dam who excelled over six furlongs as a juvenile, she's fancied to open her account for a shrewd yard; a rating of 86 makes her the one to beat in this field.

runners_data.name: Viking Barbie
runners_data.comment: Quickly into action again just a day after her latest start, she ran to form when second, beaten a length and a quarter, in a novice at Sandown, and remains capable of a bold effort over this sound-ground sprint trip; connections are short on form of late, but a rating of 77 keeps her as one of the leading dangers.

races.name: Matthew Ireland Memorial EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: High Hazard
runners_data.comment: Having shown improvement from his debut when a keen-going second, beaten a length and a half, in a novice at this course last time, he has a leading chance if he builds on that; effective over this trip on good ground, and with a jockey boasting a fine record here, a rating of 81 puts him firmly in this mix.

runners_data.name: Rosberg
runners_data.comment: He showed promise on his sole start, finishing fourth, beaten six lengths, in a novice at Thirsk, and with more expected as he steps forward, this trip on good ground should continue to suit; a rating of 81 makes him one of the leading dangers here.

runners_data.name: Asander
runners_data.comment: A modestly-bought son of Saxon Warrior out of a dam who excelled at middle distances, he was born in mid-February and looks up against it on his belated debut against more forward types; the lowest of our ratings here reflects a stiff task first time out.

runners_data.name: Happy Love
runners_data.comment: Bred with plenty of quality, being a half-brother to a high-class performer at 8f and out of a dam who excelled over five furlongs as a juvenile, he catches the eye on debut, sent out by a yard with a strong record in this event, having been successful in it last year; a rating of 84 puts him firmly among the leading fancies.

runners_data.name: Under Arrest
runners_data.comment: Well held throughout after racing off the pace when beaten ten lengths in a novice at Newmarket on his debut, he should have that experience to call on now, with this trip likely to suit; a rating of 76 means there's more to prove against this field.

runners_data.name: Astral Calling
runners_data.comment: Bred to be smart, being a daughter of Space Traveller and half-sister to a performer who excelled at seven furlongs, she was a notable pedigree buy and is sent out by a yard firing on all cylinders (a 28% strike rate over the last fortnight); a rating of 86 makes her the most interesting runner in this field on debut.

races.name: George Kilburn Memorial Nursery

runners_data.name: Emerald Bay
runners_data.note: Lightly raced but yet to win or place in three starts, most recently sixth at 6f on Good — her natural hold-up style is unlikely to be fully expressed here given the lack of a strong pace to chase, having been redistributed into a midfield slot the race shape doesn't truly offer her.
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held down at 5f in a novice at Windsor last time, this light-framed sort has yet to show a great deal in his starts so far; cheekpieces go on for the first time and, with the stable in good form, he could do better switching to handicaps for us at 54, though a month-plus absence since is a further concern.

runners_data.name: Farndale
runners_data.note: Three runs over 7f, with a best of fifth on Good going — Tim Easterby in solid 14-day form and Sean Kirrane takes the mount; likely to race in a genuine hold-up position here given her record and may pick off tiring rivals late without being a natural match-winner.
runners_data.comment: A slow start undid her chance at Chester latest, where she was ultimately well beaten in a seller, and results have been modest in her starts so far; bred to stay well and already proven over today's trip, she nonetheless remains difficult to fully trust for us at 65 as she steps into handicap company for the first time.

runners_data.name: Amantha
runners_data.note: Bolted up over 7f on Good at her most recent start, giving her the standout live form in this field; Brian Ellison's yard is quiet in the 14-day window but Pierre-Louis Jamin rides, and her four sim-going runs include a win and a place — the trip and conditions suit her better than any rival.
runners_data.comment: Stepping up having recently landed a seller by a short head at Musselburgh, she's clearly come forward with that drop in grade and looks the type to take well to handicaps on debut in that sphere; suited by 7f on a sound surface, she rates the one to beat for us at 69 in a modest race, though the yard's recent cold spell is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Tiger In The Tree
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has shaped with promise early but faded in all three starts — the uncontested lead over 7½f on fast ground is his best opportunity to control the race, though his finishing tendency is a concern against anything with class sitting just behind him; Duran Fentiman will need to judge the fractions carefully.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well back in a novice at Redcar most recently, she has struggled to make an impression in her starts to date; by a sprinting sire out of a mare suited by a mile, today's trip fits the pedigree, but on the evidence so far she's up against it for us at 45 as she tries handicaps for the first time.

runners_data.name: Happy Humpo
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field and has faded in both recent outings — a natural hold-up horse pushed into a midfield role by the race shape, compounding a style-fit discount; Cieren Fallon takes the ride but Clover's stable has minimal 14-day firepower and headgear on a horse yet to show any win or place form is not a strong sign.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten run in a maiden at Lingfield last time fell short of her seller-class form, continuing a modest start; sharper at 6f on good ground and fitted with cheekpieces for the first time, this light-framed sort looks the type to do better now she meets handicap company for us at 62, though it's been a month since that below-par effort.

races.paceDynamic: Tiger In The Tree is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and looks set to dictate from the front at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 7½f on Good to Firm ground at Beverley. With no genuine rival willing to press from the outside, Tiger In The Tree can control the fractions through the long Beverley straight, which historically rewards horses who travel prominently and save energy for the home turn. Emerald Bay and Happy Humpo are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because this field has more rear-end types than the race shape can accommodate at the back — neither is likely to find their natural rear position with so few setting the tempo ahead. This shape — a lone, uncontested pace-setter on a track that punishes late closers — strongly favours those able to track Tiger In The Tree closely in second or third, with Amantha, carrying the best recent form, best positioned to exploit a sustained-tempo scenario from just off the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Pacer Dictates Freely
scenarios.trigger: If Tiger In The Tree leads uncontested and controls a steady, honest gallop throughout the 7½f.
scenarios.body: If Tiger In The Tree leads uncontested and controls a steady, honest gallop throughout the 7½f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Runs Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If Tiger In The Tree fades dramatically in the final furlong after being let bowl along unchallenged.
scenarios.body: If Tiger In The Tree fades dramatically in the final furlong after being let bowl along unchallenged.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Tiger In The Tree is tracked at close quarters by a rival who then produces a decisive turn of foot entering the straight.
scenarios.body: If Tiger In The Tree is tracked at close quarters by a rival who then produces a decisive turn of foot entering the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses sharply and the redistributed hold-up types find their natural closing run materialises.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses sharply and the redistributed hold-up types find their natural closing run materialises.

watchPoints.text: Watch Tiger In The Tree's early sections — if Duran Fentiman sets an overly generous tempo unchallenged, Amantha tracking in second could deliver a telling move entering Beverley's straight.

Emerald Bay and Happy Humpo are natural hold-up horses who are unlikely to get that role in a slowly-run race — monitor their positioning at the start; if neither can settle at the rear of a compressed field, their chance diminishes further.

Tiger In The Tree has a recorded fading pattern in all three starts — if the leader hits the straight with a clear advantage but visibly shortens stride, the race could be taken apart by a closer in the final 2f.

Amantha is the only runner with a win in the last five outings and the only one with multiple sim-going runs in her recent history — her freshness (12 days since last run) could be an asset if the stable intended a quick follow-up on the back of that win.

Beverley's 7½f is a unique track shape with a pronounced uphill finish — horses that conserve energy tracking the pace rather than being detached are historically favoured, which reinforces the premium on those positioned second or third from the front in this low-tempo scenario.

races.name: Charlie Wood Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Al Aasy
runners_data.note: William Haggas's nine-year-old holds a clear tactical edge as the lone confirmed front-runner; he won over 12f on Soft last time out and his similar-going record is solid (10/15), though his recent form (7159-2) is patchy and he is technically racing slightly out of role at P, which marginally tempers confidence despite the favourable race shape.
runners_data.comment: Talented but sometimes hard to fathom, he returned from a short break to finish runner-up in a Group 3 at Newbury; this quick-ground test over a trip he handles well suits, and a rating of 120 makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: By The Book
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's five-year-old arrives 98 days fresh with a smart form profile (includes a 12f win on Good) and acts well on similar ground (6/7); in truth a front-running or prominent horse by inclination, he has been pushed into a midfield mapping here because there simply isn't room for him to express that style, and he will need to make the best of tracking Al Aasy rather than leading.
runners_data.comment: Back from a short break, he was below form at the top level when well held in a Group 1 at Meydan; now stepping down in grade over a trip he stays and ground he handles, a rating of 115 makes him a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Involvement
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's five-year-old is in strong recent form (T14:5/22) and ran just 27 days ago, giving him a fitness edge; he is at heart an up-with-the-pace type whose natural forward style has been squeezed out by the race shape, so Oisin Orr will need to settle him mid-division and produce a run from a position that doesn't suit him ideally.
runners_data.comment: He was well beaten in a Listed race at Goodwood last time, unable to last out 12 furlongs on the softer ground, though quicker conditions today may help him see out the same trip more effectively, aided by a jockey with a fine record at this course; stamina remains the obvious question given his figures suggest he's sharper around 10 furlongs, but a rating of 107 keeps him firmly in this mix.

runners_data.name: Miss Wong
runners_data.note: David Simcock's four-year-old is the race's genuine hold-up horse and wears a hood (hg:p); her OR of 84 makes her the least exposed on paper in terms of class, her best form (2/12f/GOO, 1/12f/SOF) has come when able to close late, but she needs a fast enough pace to exploit from off the heels and 42 days off may sharpen her.
runners_data.comment: She raced up to her mark without truly seeing out 14 furlongs when well beaten in a Group 3 at York last time, and steps back into handicap company sporting first-time cheekpieces; this shorter 12-furlong trip should suit, and a rating of 100 puts her firmly among the contenders.

runners_data.name: Percy's Daydream
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old is the freshest runner in the field at just 11 days since his last run, posting four wins this season on Good ground; like By The Book and Involvement, he is a natural prominent racer whose preferred position at the front of the pack cannot be accommodated, and Mark Winn will have to adapt his ride from a more restrained starting point than this horse ideally wants.
runners_data.comment: Progressive and race-fit having won a handicap at this course by four lengths last time, she nonetheless faces a stiff step up in grade here and, on a rating of 100, appears to have a good deal of improvement to find against this level of opposition, even with the trip and ground both in her favour.

runners_data.name: Phantom Flight
runners_data.note: Listed as a NON-RUNNER; no tactical consideration required, but his absence removes the one horse (OR 110, four wins on similar going, 14/15 on Good-equivalent surfaces) who might have tested Al Aasy for the lead and materially shaped this race differently.

races.paceDynamic: Al Aasy is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Phantom Flight a non-runner, will set sail from the front without any genuine challenger for the lead, creating a controlled, owner-dictated gallop at Beverley's 1m4f trip on Good to Firm ground. The field nominally holds several prominent types — By The Book, Involvement, and Percy's Daydream — but all three are redistributed to midfield on the pace map because they simply cannot all hold a forward position behind Al Aasy simultaneously, leaving Al Aasy alone to set the fractions he chooses. This is a textbook lone-leader scenario on a fair, fast surface: Al Aasy will control tempo from the front, with the compressed midfield group forced to track him rather than pressure him, meaning the race turns into a test of finishing quality rather than attrition. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape heavily favours the front-runner and horses with a high cruising gear who can track and quicken from a close-up position, while true hold-up horses and those forced out of their natural role face an uphill task.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Al Aasy dictates an unchallenged, measured gallop and his rivals cannot close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Al Aasy dictates an unchallenged, measured gallop and his rivals cannot close the gap in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that one of the redistributed prominent types tracks Al Aasy closely and outfinishes him in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that one of the redistributed prominent types tracks Al Aasy closely and outfinishes him in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If Al Aasy's unchallenged lead produces a false pace that collapses in the final stages, inviting a late challenge.
scenarios.body: If Al Aasy's unchallenged lead produces a false pace that collapses in the final stages, inviting a late challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types jostle for position early, disrupting the race shape and producing a messy, tactical race with no clear beneficiary.
scenarios.body: If multiple prominent types jostle for position early, disrupting the race shape and producing a messy, tactical race with no clear beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Al Aasy's unchallenged front-running position is the race's defining factor — if Cieren Fallon controls the gallop perfectly, rivals may find they have nothing left to throw at him entering the final two furlongs.

By The Book and Involvement were both mapped to midfield against their natural inclinations — watch for an early crowding incident as these horses attempt to reclaim forward positions behind Al Aasy in the first quarter-mile.

Miss Wong needs a strong pace to close into; if Al Aasy sets a falsely slow gallop from the front, Connor Beasley's hold-up tactic could leave her with too much ground to make up against fresher legs.

Percy's Daydream's fitness angle (LR:11d, four wins in recent form) is noteworthy — if the race deteriorates into a stamina test in the final furlong, his sharpness could see him outfinish the more prominent types who have been racing out of their preferred style.

races.name: Weatherbys Global Stallions App Coconut Cup Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Lexington Express
runners_data.note: Progressive 3yo with back-to-back wins over this trip and similar ground; P J McDonald booking adds confidence, and a prominent racing style suits a Porth Eilian-led tempo perfectly — strong placed form at 8f on similar going reinforces the profile.
runners_data.comment: A confirmed front-runner who sets a strong pace, she failed to last home when fourth, beaten 11 lengths, from an identical mark last time, but dropping back in trip today should suit a filly who likes to dictate up front on a sound surface, and first-time cheekpieces may sharpen her further.

runners_data.name: Enamorus
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr takes the ride on this Hugo Palmer 3yo who has shown ability at shorter but is now stepping into 1m½f territory; recent form at 7f on good ground includes placed efforts, and the uncertain style (U) leaves her tactical position open — will need to find her feet at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, she was below form down the field in a handicap at Sandown last time, but her official mark has eased, cheekpieces go on for the first time, and a jockey with a fine record at this course takes the ride; a rating of 84 suggests she's better than that effort and can play a leading role.

runners_data.name: Come On Eibhlin
runners_data.note: True hold-up filly who has been consistent at 7-8f on good ground with three placed efforts in her last four; Stevie Donohoe rides and the 9-day turnaround is short but Dylan Cunha is in decent form (3/23 T14) — needs pace to close into at Beverley's stiff finish.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her recent starts, she raced keenly but ran to form when beaten two lengths off a pound higher mark at Newmarket last time, and with the trip and surface both to suit, she can go well again; a rating of 79 keeps her right in this competitive heat.

runners_data.name: Cancelled
runners_data.note: Veteran 5yo handicapper carrying 142lbs which is a significant burden; genuine hold-up style and 48 days off could mean she returns a touch rusty, though she has placed at 9-10f on good ground and the Jonjo/A J O'Neill yard is hitting form (1/17 T14) — weight is the primary concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her recent starts, she was below form when well beaten in a handicap at Hamilton last time, but first-time cheekpieces plus a trip and surface she handles well could spark improvement; drawn wide in a field of ten, she needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Alessia Fernanda
runners_data.note: Won off this mark over 8f on standard going but recent Beverley run (6th, 7f, good) suggests the course is not a banker; 12-day turnaround on a 6yo with tongue tie keeps connections active, and she needs to replicate her winning form at 8f rather than the 7f outings.
runners_data.comment: Her form has been up and down, and she raced too keenly from off the pace when well beaten last time off a mark one pound higher than today's; drawn wide and effective around this 7-9 furlong range, first-time tongue-tie may help settle her, but on a rating of 74 she remains hard to trust on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Porth Eilian
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and sole confirmed pace-setter in this field — Edward Bethell's 3yo won over 8f on good ground and Connor Beasley partners her; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) notes she is racing slightly out of role at this trip, but her ability to dictate from the front is the defining tactical fact of this race.
runners_data.comment: She confirmed her form when third, beaten four lengths, from an identical mark last time, and with the trip and surface both suiting again on this sound going, she looks capable of running well once more; a rating of 85 puts her firmly among the leading contenders.

runners_data.name: Sandy Craic
runners_data.note: David O'Meara 3yo with a win over 7f on good ground and placed at 7f on good — travels prominently and will look to press for a front position; with 129lbs and good recent form (432551), she is a natural for the second prominent slot if Porth Eilian leads cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Returning to form emphatically to land a handicap by half a length off a two-pound lower mark at Carlisle last time, this filly now looks to be building confidence on the back of that success, and with conditions on this good-to-firm ground suiting, a rating of 89 puts her clear at the top of these figures.

runners_data.name: Sogniamo
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo who won over 9f on good — the step back to 1m½f is a slight query on trip, but Ben Robinson keeps the ride for O'Meara and the yard is in strong form (7/59 T14); naturally prominent and likely to feature in the early exchanges, though her redistribution from a natural front position means she may find herself doing more work than ideal.
runners_data.comment: She weakened quickly and failed to stay 10 furlongs when well beaten in a handicap at Redcar last time, and though today's step back to 8 furlongs is shorter than her best trip of 9f, it should still suit better than the longer test that undid her; drawn wide, a rating of 71 leaves her the outsider of this group on these figures.

runners_data.name: Vitality
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 3yo has placed at 8f on good and firm ground and is genuinely a prominent-style racer; Jason Hart rides but the redistribution into a midfield slot reflects that the prominent positions are already claimed — her chance depends on how smoothly she can navigate from a position further back than natural (STYLE_FIT 0.90).
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in four starts, she was below form when well held in a handicap at Nottingham on her handicap debut last time, and needs to find more on that evidence, though this trip and good ground have suited her in the past; a rating of 73 leaves her toward the foot of these figures.

runners_data.name: Ma Leila
runners_data.note: Tom Clover 3yo with limited form (three runs) showing a placed effort at 7f on soft — she is a natural prominent-style racer but the redistribution means she is unlikely to secure that position in this field; Ryan Sexton rides and the form base is thin at this trip and on faster ground, making her the most exposed runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless but with more improvement expected now she's tackling handicaps, she matched her debut level when third, beaten six and a quarter lengths, in a maiden at Thirsk last time, and with this trip and ground suiting, a rating of 80 makes her a strong contender to note.

races.paceDynamic: Porth Eilian is the confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground at Beverley over 1m½f, is likely to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a suicidal clip — this is a one-horse pace scenario. Sandy Craic, Sogniamo, and Lexington Express will press forward to dispute prominent positions, creating a small cluster behind Porth Eilian but not the kind of fierce early pressure that would string the field out or kill the pace. The result is a race likely to be run at an even tempo with a contested home straight, favouring horses that can travel handily within the first three or four and produce a sustained finish rather than a pure late burst. This race shape squarely favours prominent-to-handy types who can sit just off the pace and produce a progressive kick — genuine closers from far back will need something to go wrong up front. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred positions; Porth Eilian is best-placed to lead, with Sandy Craic and Sogniamo most likely to fill the prominent slots, pushing Vitality and Ma Leila — both true prominent racers — into roles further back than they would naturally choose.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Handy Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Porth Eilian dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the race develops into a sustained stretch duel from 2f out.
scenarios.body: If Porth Eilian dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the race develops into a sustained stretch duel from 2f out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Hotting Up, Midfield Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Sandy Craic and Sogniamo push hard for prominent ground early, creating a genuinely contested pace that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: If Sandy Craic and Sogniamo push hard for prominent ground early, creating a genuinely contested pace that stretches the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Crawl, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Porth Eilian rolls along at a very conservative clip with minimal pressure from the prominent group.
scenarios.body: If Porth Eilian rolls along at a very conservative clip with minimal pressure from the prominent group.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front group goes faster than it appears early and the hold-up horses get a clean run down the outside.
scenarios.body: If the front group goes faster than it appears early and the hold-up horses get a clean run down the outside.

watchPoints.text: Porth Eilian's gallop tempo is the race pivot — if Connor Beasley eases her into an unusually slow early pace, the entire scenario shifts toward a sprint finish that undermines her own chance and hands the race to sharper types like Enamorus or Sandy Craic.

Cancelled's 142lb top weight is the heaviest burden in the field and her 48-day absence makes it hard to assess freshness — watch how she moves through the paddock and whether Cieren Fallon drops her in or commits forward early.

Sandy Craic and Sogniamo may jostle for the same prominent position behind Porth Eilian in the early furlongs — any contact or checking could compromise both David O'Meara runners and create a gap for the hold-up horses to exploit.

Vitality and Ma Leila, both natural prominent types pushed into midfield by the race shape, are worth monitoring at the top of the straight — if either finds daylight and gets a clean run, they could outrun their mapped position, but they are working against the grain of this pace scenario.

Good to Firm conditions are confirmed for this race — any runner whose trainer or form record shows a preference for ease in the ground (Come On Eibhlin has most form on good, Enamorus has a soft-ground placed run) should be watched for whether they handle the surface with full fluency.

races.name: Weatherbys Racing Bank Handicap

runners_data.name: Capital Guarantee
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's hold-up performer has placed twice in five recent starts on similar good ground and steps back to a more suitable 7½f after struggling over longer trips; 21 days between runs is a comfortable prep and Mark Winn takes the ride on a horse whose finishing effort will depend entirely on the pace being genuine enough.
runners_data.comment: A below-form run at York last time, 21 days ago, continues a moderate spell, though he was runner-up earlier in this sequence of starts; suited by 7-8f on any going, this winless sort is hard to trust on the balance of the evidence despite a rating of 80 for us in his favour.

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's five-year-old has an excellent record in similar conditions with four wins and five places from 15 runs on good ground, and Alistair Rawlinson will be keen to press forward and use his prominent style; the step back from nine furlongs to 7½f looks an asset and 12 days since his last run suggests he arrives fresh.
runners_data.comment: A pair of wins sit among his last six starts, and he was beaten only a half-length in second last time from a mark just 1lb lower; front-running when conditions allow and effective at 7-9f on soft or good to firm, he has solid claims for us at 80 with the yard in good form, though he can also find one too many.

runners_data.name: Degale
runners_data.note: David and Nicola Barron have this horse running after just 10 days, and Dougie Costello takes over in the saddle; his true preference is to race from the rear, though the map places him in midfield given the number of hold-up types in the field — his finishing kick has been inconsistent and form figures of 603050 do not inspire confidence under any tactical configuration.
runners_data.comment: Little went right at Carlisle last time, well beaten down the field to continue an up-and-down profile of finishes; drawn wide today at 8f on a sound surface he handles, this winless sort is hard to trust for us at 71, the widest slot in the field a further complication.

runners_data.name: It Just Takes Time
runners_data.note: The race's confirmed pace-setter will bowl along from the front under Jack Garritty for Mark Walford, and his recent form shows back-to-back placed efforts over this exact 7f trip on good ground — his style_fit flag is a reminder that he is being asked to lead rather than race prominently, but as the only genuine front runner here his role is clear and unchallenged.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in his last two starts, he was beaten only a head off a mark 2lb lower last time at Thirsk; effective at 5-7f on any ground, this still-winless sort rates a strong threat again at 90 for us despite an 18-day break.

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Michael Dods sends out this six-year-old in excellent recent form, having won over 8f on good ground before placing at 8f and his headgear note confirms he wears a hood; Connor Beasley's booking adds a positive angle and his hold-up style suits a scenario where the pace is genuine enough to bring him into play in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with a first-time hood, he won three starts back and was only beaten 2l in fourth last time under an unchanged mark; effective at 6-8f on soft or good to firm, he remains fairly treated by the weights and rates a threat again for us at 82, with two so-so efforts in between the only blot.

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old has a superb recent record — two wins and seven places from 15 runs on good ground — and arrives here just three days after his last run, which carries a slight freshness query but also suggests the stable is confident he has bounced out of it well; Jason Hart will push forward and make use of his prominent style in what should be a straightforward race to navigate tactically.
runners_data.comment: Rock-solid of late with four places and a win from his last six starts, he was beaten only a half-length in second last time off an identical mark to today's; suited by 6-7f on a sound surface, he's the one to beat on our figures at 90, with a quick reappearance after just 3 days the only thing to note.

runners_data.name: Coolree
runners_data.note: Sam England's seven-year-old is a natural front-runner by inclination and has been winning and placing consistently at around a mile on good ground while wearing a tongue-tie; the race map places him in midfield given the crowding of prominent types, which means Oisin Orr may find him racing against his instincts and the style_fit discount is warranted.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with a tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time, he has two wins among his last six starts and was only beaten 2l in second last time from a mark just 1lb lower; equally happy at 8-10f in any conditions, he can build on that form again and rates a strong threat for us at 85, with the extra gear the only new variable to watch.

runners_data.name: Bajan Bandit
runners_data.note: Patrick Morris's six-year-old arrives in poor recent form — six moderate finishes including multiple starts on standard and fibresand surfaces — and the going report showing good-to-firm on turf today is markedly quicker than anything he has encountered in his last five outings; a genuine hold-up horse whose position in the race map is honest, but form and ground concern make him the hardest to support.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten effort at Nottingham last time extends a run of modest finishes, with turf form still very much unproven; better served by 7-8f and clearly happier on the all-weather, he wears a visor for the first time today but, rated 77 by us, still has plenty to find before he can be trusted.

races.paceDynamic: It Just Takes Time is the confirmed front runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in an eight-runner field, should be able to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without being harassed into setting a punishing tempo. Tattie Bogle and Highland Olly will press forward from prominent positions and may apply some pressure to the leader in the early stages, but neither is likely to force a true test of stamina over this 7½f trip on good-to-firm ground. This race shape — a controlled, single-led pace that produces a strongly-run final two furlongs — favours hold-up horses and those who can travel smoothly just off the pace before producing a sustained late run. Note that the field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate in those forward positions; Coolree, despite being a natural prominent racer, and Bajan Bandit and Degale, both genuine hold-up horses, are mapped to midfield as the race shape compresses their options — It Just Takes Time, Tattie Bogle, and Highland Olly are most likely to actually secure the forward berths.

scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Finishers Pounce

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate

scenarios.body: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the prominent horses tire, gifting the true hold-up runners an opportunity to sweep through.

scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Winner Emerges

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Tattie Bogle's return after just three days is genuine freshness or a slight fitness concern — if Jason Hart finds him flat early, Highland Olly could take a clear prominent berth and control the race from the front alongside It Just Takes Time.

Monitor Coolree's starting position and early running — Oisin Orr will likely attempt to push forward despite the redistribution, and if he successfully secures a prominent spot ahead of Highland Olly the race shape could tighten significantly and compress finishing room for the hold-up horses.

Glenfinnan's hood (headgear) is worth watching in the stalls and early stages — Connor Beasley will need him to settle cleanly if his hold-up run is to deliver in the final quarter-mile on this good-to-firm going.

The going report confirms the 5:10 race is returning good-to-firm conditions throughout the day, making it the fastest surface of the meeting — Capital Guarantee's sim-going record of 11 wins or places from 15 comparable runs suggests this ground profile suits him, and his hold-up style is precisely the profile the dominant scenario favours.

races.name: Happy Birthday Roy Archer Handicap

runners_data.name: Truly Special
runners_data.note: A hold-up filly who has shown form over 6-8f on good ground, with a recent third over 8f her best relevant piece; Connor Beasley is a strong course booking and 26 days off looks routine, but she needs cover and a true pace to be seen to best effect — the lone front-runner scenario makes her task harder.
runners_data.comment: Landing a handicap by three-quarters of a length last time from a mark 2lb lower than today's, she did so with a willing attitude that marks her the type to progress; best at 7-8f on soft or good to firm, though less effective on the all-weather, she can follow up for us at 65 if building further on that form.

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has placed four times in her last five starts, all on good or good-to-firm, and drew clear of rivals in testing conditions last time; the style-fit flag reflects OR=52 and a step up to 7½f, but with no rival to challenge her early she is in the ideal tactical position and Cieren Fallon is a top-quality booking.
runners_data.comment: Full of running when landing a handicap by a head last time from a mark 2lb lower than today's, she's rounded off that sort of form with three seconds and a win among her last six starts; suited by 6f on soft or good to firm, she's the pick for us at 69 in a modest race, though the yard's recent quiet spell is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Zoulette
runners_data.note: A hold-up type with a second over 7f on good ground last outing suggesting the trip suits, though overall consistency is limited; Stevie Donohoe retains the ride and 32 days since last run is the longest break in this field — her best chance is a stronger-than-expected pace that brings hold-up horses into play.
runners_data.comment: A well-held effort at Wolverhampton last time fell short of her best, though she was runner-up two starts earlier; suited by 5-7f on good to firm or the all-weather, this yet-to-win filly could have more to offer for us at 57 if bouncing back from a stale run after a month-plus absence.

runners_data.name: Forever Twenty
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's gelding has headgear in play and has placed over this trip on good ground, but his true style is held-up — he is placed in midfield on the map only because the rear is congested with similar types, meaning he may race further forward than comfortable; Jason Hart will need to manage the positioning carefully.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 6l when below form at Doncaster last time, she'll need to bounce back from that effort; sporting cheekpieces for the first time and suited by 7f on quick ground or the all-weather, this winless filly is up against it for us at a rating of 57 following a moderate recent sequence.

runners_data.name: Walk On Walk On
runners_data.note: Showed some ability with a fourth over 7f on good ground but has failed to build on it, and Noel Wilson's yard has gone 0/5 in the last 14 days; his natural rear-runner instinct will be constrained by the crowded hold-up profile in this field, and Ryan Sexton will have to compromise his position in a race without a strong pace.
runners_data.comment: A modest fifth beaten 6l up at 1m at Ayr last time did at least point to progress after a quiet spell; better suited back at 6-7f on any going, cheekpieces go on for the first time and, with his mark drifting lower, this winless sort for us at 56 still needs more before he can be trusted.

runners_data.name: Hood Wink
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's gelding sports a hood, has won over 8f on good ground, and boasts the strongest recent form in the field with multiple top-four finishes; though he is a natural hold-up horse bumped forward on the map by the surplus of rear-runners, his solid Beverley-track-compatible form and 1W3P on similar going makes him notable even if his position is compromised.
runners_data.comment: Consistency has been the theme lately with two thirds and a fourth, and he matched that level again in third last time, beaten 2l from a mark 1lb higher than today's; sharp at 1m on most going including the all-weather, first-time blinkers could sharpen him up further for us at 64, though he still needs to find extra to land his next win.

runners_data.name: Maid On The Shelf
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's filly has only three career runs, all over further than today's trip and on ground varying from good to soft — the step down to 7½f is a concern for a horse that hasn't placed; her prominent style slots her naturally behind Battenburg Belle and Oisin Orr is an excellent claim, but raw inexperience and limited form are significant questions.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten effort in a maiden at Hamilton latest continues a modest opening to her career, rarely threatening the front rank; bred to appreciate further ground around 10f, she may do better now she tackles handicaps for us at a rating of 46, though she still has plenty to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Battenburg Belle is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 7½f Beverley handicap and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the early lead, she is set to bowl along at a sustainable gallop from stall one on good-to-firm ground. Maid On The Shelf is the only other naturally prominent type and will slot in directly behind, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching — a controlled, even tempo is the most probable race shape. The field behind Battenburg Belle is dominated by hold-up horses — Truly Special, Zoulette, Forever Twenty, Walk On Walk On, and Hood Wink are all rear-to-midfield types — but three of them (Forever Twenty, Walk On Walk On, Hood Wink) are redistributed to midfield on the map because there are more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, so those three are unlikely to secure their natural position and may race closer than ideal. With a lone, uncontested front-runner likely to control a modest tempo on good-to-firm turf around Beverley's turning track, the race shape strongly favours horses that can race close enough to the pace to pounce in the straight — the prominent and close-tracking midfield profile is the most advantaged, not deep closers who will face a wall of quickening horses ahead of them.

scenarios.body: If Battenburg Belle is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and control a comfortable gallop throughout.

scenarios.body: If the pace proves slightly faster than expected and a close-tracking stalker picks Battenburg Belle off inside the final furlong.

scenarios.body: If Battenburg Belle goes too fast early for the small field and the pace collapses in the straight, giving genuine closers a run at the line.

scenarios.trigger: If Battenburg Belle is pressured earlier than expected or the field fails to settle and the race bunches up in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Battenburg Belle is pressured earlier than expected or the field fails to settle and the race bunches up in the straight.

watchPoints.text: Battenburg Belle — if she jumps cleanly and strides into an uncontested lead inside the first furlong, the race is effectively being run to her strengths and her four-race placed streak on similar going makes her a major danger from the front.

Hood Wink — carrying the best recent form figures in the race (three consecutive top-four finishes on good ground over 7-8f) but his hold-up style will be compromised by the congested rear; watch where Kirrane positions him in the first two furlongs to gauge whether he can race naturally.

Maid On The Shelf — Oisin Orr on a Charlie Johnston runner dropping in trip with only three runs to her name is worth monitoring in the market; if she's drifting she's unproven, if she's shortening Johnston may know more than the bare form suggests.

Forever Twenty and Walk On Walk On — both true hold-up horses shuffled forward on the pace map, creating a real risk of positional congestion in the midfield early on; if they race awkwardly or lose rhythm in the first quarter-mile their chances are largely extinguished regardless of ability.
